craft_notes: Sthāyin: māda-vīra of holy drunkenness; vyabhicāri mattollāsa at burnt bonds. Sanskrit-first: bandha-mārga (BOND-ROADS — kept; roads are walked); stuti-agni (PRAISE-FIRE — kept); mada (MAD-DRUNK — kept raw). Rows: 9 (shake/drink/burnt triad — three verbs, one breath), 1 (‘bliss is mine’ closes — intoxication owned last). Close: ‘bliss is mine’. Rupture: semicolon (burnt turns to drunk — purification turns to joy). Rejected: ‘paths’ for roads — killed: roads walked; ‘wine’ for glory's rush — killed: mahimā-vega kept (rush, not wine). Read aloud: SHAKE-off THE-bond-ROADS, DRINK-deep OF-things — BURNT-clean IN-praise-FIRE … MAD-drunk ON-glo-ry's-RUSH, O-giv-ER — BLISS is-MINE.

lines: Shake off the bond-roads, drink deep of things — burnt clean in praise-fire;
mad-drunk on glory's rush, O giver — bliss is mine.

reads_against.argmap: What does the shaken-off sing? → Bond burnt, glory rushed, things drunk: madness-bliss sings.
c1_essence: Bond-conceit shaken, difference burnt, glory drunk: madness-bliss.
